chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was in the lap of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when he raised his head and said, 'O Father, what is for the one who visits you after your death?' He said, 'O my son, whoever comes to me as a visitor after my death, for him is Paradise; and whoever comes to your father is, whoever visits him after his death, for him is Paradise; and whoever your brother is, whoever visits him after his death, for him is Paradise; and whoever you are, whoever visits you after your death, for him is Paradise.'

key_terms.أَخَاكَ: your brother (referring to Imam Hasan or Husayn)
key_terms.زِيَارَة: visitation (specifically to graves or shrines of the righteous)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Imams after their death?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a unique spiritual merit where visiting the Prophet, Imam Hasan, Imam Husayn, and the Imams themselves after their death guarantees Paradise. This narration underscores the Shia concept of *Ziyarat* as an act of worship that maintains the living connection between the faithful and the Ahl al-Bayt, extending the reward of companionship beyond the grave.
